paragraphs: Art. 1. (1) This ordinance sets the conditions and procedure for competitions for notaries.
(2) The competitions are organised and funded by the Ministry of Justice.
Art. 3. (1) The competition consists of a written and an oral exam.
(2) The questions are set from the indicative list of topics in the annex; they may be cases from notarial practice.
(3) Candidates may use legal acts and case law on paper. A candidate who uses other aids is removed from the competition.

8.title: Written exam
paragraphs: Art. 8. (1) The commission prepares three variants of questions for the written exam.
(2) Before the exam, the commission gives each candidate a form, white sheets stamped with the seal of the Ministry of Justice, and two opaque envelopes, A4 and A5.
(3) After the start is announced, a candidate chosen at random draws one variant and announces it.
(4) The written exam is held at the same time for all candidates, in one or more rooms, in the presence of invigilators.
(5) The written exam lasts three hours; the chair announces its start and end.
(6) The work is written on the sheets received, only with a blue pen.
(7) After finishing, each candidate writes his full name, personal number and the date on the form and seals it in the small envelope.
(8) The work and the small envelope are sealed in the large envelope by the candidate in the presence of a commission member; the candidate and the member sign a list.
(9) After the exam the full commission opens the large envelopes at random and writes the same number on the small envelope, the large envelope and the work.
(10) The commission grades the works under Art. 10(1) and (2), then checks the small envelopes, opens them, identifies the works and records the grades.
(11) The sheets and envelopes must carry no marks identifying the candidate; otherwise the candidate's exam is annulled with a protocol.
(12) The results are posted in the Ministry of Justice and on its website.

9.title: Oral exam
paragraphs: Art. 9. (1) Candidates who passed the written exam with at least good (4) are admitted to the oral exam.
(2) The commission prepares a list and a schedule, posted five days before the oral exam in the Ministry and on its website.
(3) Candidates who did not appear on schedule may appear on the same or the next exam day after the others.
(4) Each candidate draws a ticket with a question; its number is recorded in the protocol.
(5) The oral exam is held before the commission, a stenographer and up to 5 following candidates.

10.title: Grading and ranking
paragraphs: Art. 10. (1) The written exam is graded poor (2), satisfactory (3), good (4), very good (5) or excellent (6).
(2) Each member records his grades in the protocol under Art. 8(10), signed, dated and handed to the chair. The result is the arithmetic mean of all members' grades.
(3) The oral exam is graded on the same scale.
(4) Each member records his oral grade; the result is the mean, announced immediately and recorded by the chair.
(5) Candidates with at least good (4) in both exams are ranked for the places by the mean of the two grades.

11.title: Protocol of ranking
paragraphs: Art. 11. (1) A protocol of the ranking is made in three copies signed by all members. One copy is sent to the Minister of Justice within 7 days of the end of the exam; the others stay with the competition records.
(2) An extract is posted in the Ministry, published on its website and sent to the Notary Chamber.
(3) On the protocol, the Minister of Justice issues an order under Art. 12 of the Notaries Act for the entry of each ranked candidate in the register of the Notary Chamber.
(4) After the competition, all records are handed to the archive of the Ministry of Justice.
